# Big-O Notation

Big-O notation describes the upper bound of an algorithm's time or space complexity as the input size grows. Common classes: O(1) constant, O(log n) logarithmic (binary search), O(n) linear, O(n log n) efficient sorting, O(n^2) nested loops, O(2^n) brute force. We ignore constants and lower-order terms: 3n + 5 simplifies to O(n). Big-O focuses on scalability, not exact runtime.
